q: Ammonia or HFC refrigeration for a new cold storage: what is the carbon difference?
title: Ammonia or HFC for a new cold store
short: Ammonia leaks add no CO2e, while every kilogram of R-404A that leaks adds about 4.7 tonnes of CO2e. A 500 kg R-404A charge losing 10% a year adds about 236 tonnes of CO2e a year. Electricity is the other half, so compare both systems' annual kWh before deciding.
audience: Cold storage investors and agri processors

sections.h: Where the carbon difference comes from
ul: Leaks: refrigerant lost through joints, valves and servicing is a direct Scope 1 emission, counted as kilograms lost x the gas's GWP.
Electricity: compressors, fans and pumps run all year, and their kWh are Scope 2 at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh on the Indian grid.
Ammonia (R-717) is not a Kyoto gas and IPCC AR6 gives it no GWP, so its leaks count as zero CO2e. The choice then turns on electricity.

sections.h: How the R-404A figure is worked out
p: R-404A is a blend, so its GWP is the mass-weighted sum of its parts, using IPCC AR6 100-year values: 44% HFC-125 at 3,740, 52% HFC-143a at 5,810 and 4% HFC-134a at 1,530. That gives 0.44 x 3,740 + 0.52 x 5,810 + 0.04 x 1,530 = 1,645.6 + 3,021.2 + 61.2 = 4,728. Lower-GWP HFC and HFO blends sold as R-404A replacements cut this, but not to zero; work out their GWP the same way from the supplier's composition.

sections.h: Why the HFC phase-down matters for a 20-year asset
p: Under the Kigali Amendment India, an Article 5 Group 2 country, freezes HFC consumption in 2028 and then steps it down until 2047, when it reaches 15% of the baseline. A cold store commissioned now will still need top-up gas in the 2040s, when far less HFC can be sold in India. Ammonia sits outside the phase-down. The full step-by-step schedule is on our Kigali page linked below.

sections.h: How to compare two quotes fairly
ol: Ask each vendor for the refrigerant, charge in kg and expected annual kWh at your design load and ambient temperature.
Estimate leaks as charge x an annual leak rate. Use your own service history if you have it; otherwise label it an estimate.
Add pump energy for any glycol or CO2 secondary loop used with ammonia; it is part of the ammonia system's kWh.
Compare total annual CO2e: leak kg x GWP plus kWh x 0.710.
p: Ammonia is toxic, so plant room design, trained operators and local safety approvals are part of the decision. They are outside this carbon comparison.

example.title: Worked example: 500 kg R-404A charge against ammonia
lines: R-404A charge 500 kg, annual leak 10% (illustrative) = 50 kg
Leak emissions: 50 x 4,728 = 236,400 kg, about 236.4 t CO2e a year
Electricity, both systems assumed at 1,000,000 kWh a year: 1,000,000 x 0.710 = 710,000 kg, 710 t CO2
HFC system: 236.4 + 710 = 946.4 t CO2e a year; ammonia system: 710 t
If the ammonia system used 10% more electricity: 1,100,000 x 0.710 = 781 t, still 165.4 t a year lower
Break-even: the ammonia system could use 236,400 / 0.710 = 332,958 kWh more a year, about 33% more here, before the HFC system has the lower total
example.note: Leak rate and electricity use are assumptions for the arithmetic. Industrial refrigeration leak rates vary widely with design and maintenance; use your vendors' figures.

senseible: Senseible turns a refrigerant top-up invoice into Scope 1 CO2e once the gas and the kilograms charged are given, and counts the cold store's grid power in Scope 2 at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, so after commissioning you can see whether leaks or electricity drive the footprint. The comparison before purchase uses your vendors' own figures.
